claims: The United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is the primary federal law enforcement arm of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS investigates over 200 mail-related federal crimes.
Postal Inspectors are armed federal agents.
Postal Inspectors ensure the integrity of the nation's 30,000+ postal facilities.
USPIS investigates the theft of mail.
USPIS investigates mail fraud.
USPIS investigates prohibited mailings (drugs, explosives).
USPIS investigates dangerous mail.
USPIS protects postal employees and customers from violence and threats, including robberies.
Postal Inspectors have authority to serve warrants.
Postal Inspectors have authority to serve subpoenas.
Postal Inspectors have authority to make arrests for postal-related crimes.
USPIS protects the infrastructure of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS protects the revenue of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS protects the assets of the U.S. Postal Service.
USPIS was founded in 1775.
USPIS is the oldest federal law enforcement agency in the U.S.
Besides Postal Inspectors, USPIS utilizes Postal Police Officers to secure high-value facilities and assets.
USPIS operates nationwide and internationally.
USPIS has inspectors in every state to support investigations.
Postal Inspectors combat identity theft.
